```{r setup, include=FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(echo = TRUE)
library(MASS)
```

### Set up

This simulation will not use explicit spatial representation of the porpoise positions instead we will use distributional shapes and draw frm the

Number of animals: 1000
transect width:150
Number of variables in theta: 5

```{r}
N <- 1000
w <- 150
theta_length <- 5
```


### 1. Define the distribution of $f(y)$ and $f(\Theta)$

$f(y)$ and $f(\Theta)$ are  the distribution of the horizontal distacnes to the transects  and the joint distribution of the covariates $\theta$ before sampling.  We will assume both to be independent of each other so that we can write the joint distribution as $f(y,\Theta) = f(y)f(\Theta)$. For the case of $f(y)$ we will assume a uniform distribution between 0 and $w$ this is we assume that the placement of the transects does not depend on the distribution of the animals. For the case of $f(\Theta)$ for now we will assume$\Theta$ has 5 components, we will assume a multivariate normal distribution with mean vector $\mu$ and covariance matrix $\Sigma$ assuming no correlation between the variables of $\Theta$.

```{r }
f_y <- runif(1000, 0, w)
f_theta <- mvrnorm(n = 1000, mu = rep(0, theta_length), Sigma = diag(theta_length))
```

## Defining the detection function

We will define the detection function in a reduced Sobol decomposition form (reduced here means that we will not include the interaction terms within the covariates). The decompositions looks like this:

$$g(y, \Theta) = g_0 + g_y(y) + g_\theta(\theta) + g_{y,\theta}(y, \theta)$$

Where $g_0$ is the average detection probability across all $y$ and all $\Theta$ ($P_c$), and the variance of the detection function is given by:

$$Var(g(y, \Theta)) = Var(g_y(y)) + Var(g_\theta(\theta)) + Var(g_{y,\theta}(y, \theta))$$
